image_description: A large sturgeon swimming in an aquarium tank, viewed through glass. The fish has a dark gray/brown dorsal side and lighter ventral side. Visible features include the elongated body, pointed snout, heterocercal tail, and rows of bony scutes along the lateral line and back. The background shows a sandy bottom with rocks and another fish in the distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly elongated and the mouth position appears to be on the underside (ventral), consistent with sturgeon anatomy, though the exact protrusion is hard to see due to angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The resolution and water distortion near the snout make it impossible to definitively count or identify four distinct barbels. They are not clearly visible.
The snout is distinctly pointed and elongated, matching the diagnostic feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is clearly elongated and fusiform, taking up a significant portion of the frame, indicating large proportions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of bony plates (scutes) are visible along the lateral line and dorsal ridge. While counting exactly five rows is difficult due to perspective, the presence of this specific texture instead of scales is clear.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish exhibits clear countershading: dark gray/brown on top and a significantly lighter, whitish/cream color on the belly.
The tail fin is clearly asymmetrical, with the upper lobe being larger and extending further than the lower lobe, which is the definition of heterocercal.

Natural depth-of-field blur and water turbidity cause the background elements to be indistinct. This is consistent with a real photograph.
